text: Old Koskoosh. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had once been a great hunter. <break time="0.8s" /> And the chief of his tribe. <break time="0.8s" /> Sat by a small fire. <break time="0.8s" /> And listened greedily. <break time="0.8s" /> His eyes had grown dim long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> But his hearing was still sharp. <break time="0.8s" /> And every sound told him. <break time="0.8s" /> What was happening. <break time="0.8s" /> It was the sound of his own tribe. <break time="0.8s" /> Breaking camp. <break time="0.8s" /> For they were going on a long journey. <break time="0.8s" /> Without him. <break time="0.8s" /> He heard Sit cum to ha. <break time="0.8s" /> His sons daughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Shouting at the dogs. <break time="0.8s" /> And pushing them into their harnesses. <break time="0.8s" /> He heard his sons voice. <break time="0.8s" /> Ordering the women to hurry. <break time="0.8s" /> And the medicine man grunting. <break time="0.8s" /> As he loaded the last tent. <break time="0.8s" /> Onto a sled. <break time="0.8s" /> Somewhere a child was crying. <break time="0.8s" /> And Koskoosh thought. <break time="0.8s" /> That little Koo tee. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was weak and often sick. <break time="0.8s" /> Might not live long. <break time="0.8s" /> The tribe had to move quickly. <break time="0.8s" /> Because the winter day was short. <break time="0.8s" /> And the long trail would not wait. <break time="0.8s" /> Koskoosh did not blame them. <break time="0.8s" /> For he knew that an old man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who could not keep up. <break time="0.8s" /> Would only slow the whole tribe down. <break time="0.8s" /> He had lived his life. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was the young, not the old. <break time="0.8s" /> Who needed the food and the strength now.
